Plot prediction accuracy as a function of model strength

plot_accuracy_vs_strength.Rd

A calibration/psychometric-function style plot of how often a model's predicted winner matches the actual (e.g. human) choice, as a function of a continuous measure of how "easy" the triplet should be – typically model.strength()'s distance-ratio metric, or (when model.strength() is called with its own alpha argument set) the choice-model probability of the predicted winner. Shows the raw per-triplet outcomes, Wilson-score binned accuracy with confidence intervals, and (optionally) a fitted binomial GLM curve, all on one plot.

Usage

plot_accuracy_vs_strength(
  strength,
  accuracy,
  n_bins = 10,
  binning = c("quantile", "equal_width"),
  ci_level = 0.95,
  glm = TRUE,
  show_raw = TRUE,
  xlab = "Model strength",
  ylab = "P(correct)",
  main = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

strength

Numeric vector giving each triplet's model-strength value (e.g. the output of model.strength()).

accuracy

Vector the same length as strength: 1/TRUE if the model's predicted winner matched the actual choice on that triplet, 0/FALSE otherwise.

n_bins

Number of bins along the strength axis (default 10). See binning.

binning

"quantile" (default) puts roughly equal numbers of triplets in each bin, which keeps a bin's point from being a sparse-data artifact even when strength values cluster (e.g. most triplets near 1.0 for a good embedding). "equal_width" instead divides the observed range of strength into n_bins equal-width bins – more interpretable x-axis spacing, at the cost of some bins potentially having very few or no points.

ci_level

Confidence level for each bin's Wilson score interval (default 0.95).

glm

Logical; if TRUE (default), fits accuracy ~ strength as a binomial GLM and overlays its predicted curve.

show_raw

Logical; if TRUE (default), plots the raw 0/1 outcomes, jittered vertically, as a light background layer so the binned summary isn't the only thing shown.

xlab, ylab, main, ...

Passed to the underlying plot() call.

Value

Invisibly, a list with bins (the per-bin summary data frame: strength, n, n_correct, p_correct, ci_lower, ci_upper) and glm_fit (the fitted glm object, or NULL if glm = FALSE).

Details

Binned proportions use the Wilson score interval rather than a naive phat +/- 1.96*SE interval, since the latter can extend outside [0, 1] or be badly too narrow exactly where this plot is most informative: bins near strength = 1 where the model should rarely be wrong, so the observed proportion of errors in that bin is small and its naive SE is an unreliable guide to the uncertainty.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 300
strength <- runif(n, 0.5, 1)
# Simulated probability of a correct prediction that increases with
# strength, for a plausible example.
p_true <- 0.5 + 0.45 * (strength - 0.5) / 0.5
accuracy <- rbinom(n, 1, p_true)

plot_accuracy_vs_strength(strength, accuracy)
